title: Greedy: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
oneLiner: The largest sum of any contiguous run: a running sum that has gone negative only drags the next element down, so drop it and start fresh.
keyTakeaway: Keep current, the best sum of a run ENDING at i: current = max(nums[i], current + nums[i]). That says "extend the run if what came before helps, otherwise start over here". The answer is the best current seen. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space, and it handles all-negative arrays if you start from nums[0] rather than 0.
explanation:
Given an integer array, return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray (a run of neighbouring elements). For [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] the answer is 6, from [4, -1, 2, 1].

Trying every start and end is O(n^2) even with a running sum. Kadane's algorithm does it in one pass by asking a smaller question at each index: what is the best sum of a run that ENDS exactly here? Call it current. A run ending at i is either nums[i] alone or the best run ending at i - 1 with nums[i] tacked on, so current = max(nums[i], current + nums[i]). The overall answer is the largest current you ever see.

The greedy reading of the same line: if the running sum before i is negative, it can only make anything after it smaller, so throw it away and restart at i. Keeping a negative prefix is never better, which is the exchange argument in one sentence. (It's also the simplest example of dynamic programming: current is dp[i], and only the previous cell is ever needed, so the table shrinks to one variable.)

Start both current and best at nums[0], not at 0. With [-3, -1, -2] the answer is -1 (the subarray must be non-empty); starting best at 0 would wrongly return 0.

Overflow: the sum of many large ints can pass int.MaxValue (2,147,483,647) in C#, where int arithmetic silently wraps round to negative numbers unless you use long or a checked block. Python ints never overflow. The tests here stay inside int range.

The visualization walks the example; the tracker is best, and the highlighted cells are the run that current is summing.

recognitionSignals: "Largest / maximum sum of a contiguous subarray" (or the stock-profit variant: the largest rise between two days).
Negative numbers are allowed, so a sliding window can't decide when to shrink.
Each position's best answer depends only on the previous position's best answer.
gotchas: Initialise with nums[0], not 0, or an all-negative array returns 0 instead of its largest element.
Update best after updating current at every index, not only when you restart.
Restart when current + nums[i] < nums[i] (equivalently, when current < 0), not when nums[i] is negative: a negative element inside a good run is fine.
confusableWith: Sliding Window: works for max sum of a FIXED-size window or when all numbers are positive; with negatives and any length, Kadane's is the tool.
Prefix Sums: the best subarray is the largest prefix[j] - prefix[i]; tracking the smallest prefix so far gives the same O(n) answer.
Gas Station (this track) uses the same "a negative running sum is never worth keeping" restart.

complexity.note: Kadane's algorithm: one pass with two variables, the best run ending here and the best overall.

referenceSolutions.python:
def max_sub_array(nums):
    current = best = nums[0]
    for x in nums[1:]:
        # Extend the run ending at the previous element, or start fresh if that run is a drag.
        current = max(x, current + x)
        best = max(best, current)
    return best
